newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-DEVERS EASES WAY THROUGH FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DEVERS EASES WAY THROUGH FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Olympic 100 metres champion Gail Devers eased her way through the first of three rounds of the women's 60 metres scheduled for the opening day of the world indoor championships on Friday.
Devers, the 1993 world indoor champion, won her heat while slowing down in 7.21 seconds.
"I'm feeling my way through the rounds just to get through to the finals injury free," the American explained.

Devers's fingernails, so long they seemed more like talons than nails and painted a lurid shade of blue, excited more attention than her running. The trackside television camera lingered on Devers's hands as she composed herself at the start and again after she finished.
"I'm about to cut them," she said. "I've had them for a long time, it's time to start over."
World record holder Irina Privalova of Russia, a world indoor champion over three separate distances, was equally untroubled in winning her heat in 7.27 seconds.

Earlier on a fine Parisian spring morning Ato Boldon rubbed the sleep from his eyes in time to qualify comfortably for the men's 200 metres semifinals on the opening day of the world indoor championships.

Boldon, bronze medallist in both the 100 and 200 metres at last year's Atlanta Olympics and the fastest man in the world this year, finished second in his first round heat behind Chile's Sebastian Keitel, bronze medallist at the 1995 world championships. Both men clocked 20.99 seconds.
The 23-year-old Trinidadian, one of a number of athletes who found it necessary to wear sunglasses inside the Bercy stadium, complained later of the early start.
"It's hard to run this early in the morning," Boldon said. "The track's not that fast, there's no bounce in it.
American champion Rohsaan Griffin, suffering from the additional handicap of jet-lag, still managed to win his heat in 20.85 seconds.
"My body hasn't woken up yet," he said. "It's still three in the morning for me."
In the women's first round heats jamaican Juliet Cuthbert, double silver medallist at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, clocked the year's second fastest time of 22.76 seconds.
American Chryste Gaines finished fifth and last behind Cuthbert but still managed to qualify for Friday evening's semifinals as one of the eight fastest losers.
